sanskrit: atha tasyām avasthāyāṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ rāvaṇānujaḥ pareṣām ahitaṃ vākyam arthasādhakam abravīt
english: Then, in that situation, the younger brother of Rāvaṇa [Vibhīṣaṇa] spoke to Lakṣmaṇa words that were purposeful and harmful to the enemy.

sanskrit: asyānīkasya mahato bhedane yatalakṣmaṇa rākṣasendrasuto 'py atra bhinne dṛśyo bhaviṣyati
english: "Strive, O Lakṣmaṇa, to break through this great army — when it is broken, the son of the lord of rākṣasas will become visible here."

sanskrit: sa tvam indrāśaniprakhyaiḥ śarair avakiran parān abhidravāśu yāvad vai naitat karma samāpyate
english: "Therefore, showering the foes with arrows like unto Indra's thunderbolts, charge swiftly until this task is accomplished."

sanskrit: jahi vīradurātmānaṃ māyāparam adhārmikam rāvaṇiṃ krūrakarmāṇaṃ sarvalokabhayāvaham
english: "Slay Rāvaṇi — that wicked hero, that master of illusion, that unrighteous one of cruel deeds, the terror of all the worlds."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi rākṣasendrasutaṃ prati
english: Having heard Vibhīṣaṇa's words, Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks poured down showers of arrows against the son of the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: ṛkṣāḥ śākhāmṛgāś caiva drumādrivarayodhinaḥ abhyadhāvanta sahitās tad anīkam avasthitam
english: Bears and monkeys too, those foremost fighters with trees and boulders, charged together against that standing army.

sanskrit: rākṣasāś ca śitair bāṇair asibhiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ udyataiḥ samavartanta kapisainyajighāṃsavaḥ
english: And the rākṣasas, eager to slay the monkey army, came on with sharp arrows, swords, śaktis, and raised tomaras.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulaḥ saṃjajñe kapirakṣasām śabdena mahatā laṅkāṃ nādayan vai samantataḥ
english: That tumultuous clash between the monkeys and rākṣasas arose, reverberating Laṅkā on all sides with a great roar.

sanskrit: śastrair bahuvidhākāraiḥ śitair bāṇaiś ca pādapaiḥ udyatair giriśṛṅgaiś ca ghorair ākāśam āvṛtam
english: The sky was filled with weapons of many forms, with sharp arrows, uprooted trees, and dreadful mountain peaks raised aloft.

sanskrit: te rākṣasā vānareṣu vikṛtānanabāhavaḥ niveśayantaḥ śastrāṇi cakrus te sumahad bhayam
english: Those rākṣasas with distorted faces and arms, driving their weapons into the monkeys, caused them very great terror.

sanskrit: tathaiva sakalair vṛkṣair giriśṛṅgaiś ca vānarāḥ abhijaghnur nijaghnuś ca samare rākṣasarṣabhān
english: Likewise the monkeys, with whole trees and mountain peaks, struck and smote the foremost rākṣasas in battle.

sanskrit: ṛkṣavānaramukhyaiś ca mahākāyair mahābalaiḥ rakṣasāṃ vadhyamānānāṃ mahad bhayam ajāyata
english: As the rākṣasas were being slaughtered by those great-bodied, mighty-armed chiefs of bears and monkeys, a great fear arose among them.

sanskrit: svam anīkaṃ viṣaṇṇaṃ tu śrutvā śatrubhir arditam udatiṣṭhata durdharṣas tat karmaṇy ananuṣṭhite
english: But hearing that his own army was distressed and afflicted by the enemy, the invincible one arose, that task yet unaccomplished.

sanskrit: vṛkṣāndhakārān niṣkramya jātakrodhaḥ sa rāvaṇiḥ āruroha rathaṃ sajjaṃ pūrvayuktaṃ sa rākṣasaḥ
english: Emerging from the darkness of the trees, that rākṣasa Rāvaṇi, filled with fury, mounted a chariot already yoked and ready.

sanskrit: sa bhīmakārmukaśaraḥ kṛṣṇāñjanacayopamaḥ raktāsyanayanaḥ krūro babhau mṛtyur ivāntakaḥ
english: He with his dreadful bow and arrows, resembling a mass of black collyrium, with red mouth and red eyes, cruel, shone like Death himself, the Ender.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva tu rathasthaṃ taṃ paryavartata tad balam rakṣasāṃ bhīmavegānāṃ lakṣmaṇena yuyutsatām
english: And upon seeing him stationed in his chariot, that army of rākṣasas of fearful speed, eager to fight with Lakṣmaṇa, rallied about.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle tu hanumān udyamya sudurāsadam dharaṇīdharasaṃkāśī mahāvṛkṣam ariṃdamaḥ
english: At that moment Hanumān, the subduer of enemies, resembling a bearer of the earth, raising an enormous tree that was very hard to face —

sanskrit: sa rākṣasānāṃ tat sainyaṃ kālāgnir iva nirdahan cakāra bahubhir vṛkṣair niḥsaṃjñaṃ yudhi vānaraḥ
english: — that monkey, like the fire of dissolution scorching the rākṣasas' army, rendered it insensible in battle with blow after blow of trees.

sanskrit: vidhvaṃsayantaṃ tarasā dṛṣṭvaiva pavanātmajam rākṣasānāṃ sahasrāṇi hanūmantam avākiran
english: Seeing the son of the Wind-god destroying them with speed, thousands of rākṣasas showered down upon Hanumān.

sanskrit: śitaśūladharāḥ śūlair asibhiś cāsipāṇayaḥ śaktibhiḥ śaktihastāś ca paṭṭasaiḥ paṭṭasāyudhāḥ
english: Those bearing sharp tridents with their tridents, those with swords in hand with their swords, those holding śaktis with their śaktis, those armed with paṭṭasas with their paṭṭasas —

sanskrit: parighaiś ca gadābhiś ca kuntaiś ca śubhadarśanaiḥ śataśaś ca śataghnībhir āyasair api mudgaraiḥ
english: — and with iron clubs, maces, and fine-looking lances, and with hundreds of śataghnīs and iron hammers —

sanskrit: ghoraiḥ paraśubhiś caiva bhiṇḍipālaiś ca rākṣasāḥ muṣṭibhir vajravegaiś ca talair aśanisaṃnibhaiḥ
english: — and with dreadful axes and bhiṇḍipālas, and with fists swift as thunderbolts and palms like lightning-bolts, those rākṣasas struck him.

sanskrit: abhijaghnuḥ samāsādya samantāt parvatopamam teṣām api ca saṃkruddhaś cakāra kadanaṃ mahat
english: Closing in from all sides they struck the one who resembled a mountain; and upon them too, in great fury, he wrought terrible carnage.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa kapiśreṣṭham acalopamam indrajit sūdayānam amitraghnam amitrān pavanātmajam
english: Indrajit beheld the best of monkeys, the son of the Wind, steadfast as a mountain, slaying enemies and routing foes.

sanskrit: sa sārathim uvācedaṃ yāhi yatraiṣa vānaraḥ kṣayam eva hi naḥ kuryād rākṣasānām upekṣitaḥ
english: He said to his charioteer: "Drive to where that monkey is — ignored, he would bring utter destruction upon us rākṣasas."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sārathis tena yayau yatra sa mārutiḥ vahan paramadurdharṣaṃ sthitam indrajitaṃ rathe
english: Thus addressed by him, the charioteer drove to where Māruti stood, bearing the supremely invincible Indrajit in the chariot.

sanskrit: so 'bhyupetya śarān khaḍgān paṭṭasāsiparaśvadhān abhyavarṣata durdharṣaḥ kapimūrdhni sa rākṣasaḥ
english: That invincible rākṣasa, coming close, rained down upon the monkey's head arrows, swords, paṭṭasas, blades, and battle-axes.

sanskrit: tāni śastrāṇi ghorāḥ pratigṛhya sa mārutiḥ roṣeṇa mahatāviṣo vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: Receiving those dreadful weapons, Māruti, blazing with great rage, spoke these words indeed.

sanskrit: yudhyasva yadi śūro 'si rāvaṇātmaja durmate vāyuputraṃ samāsādya na jīvan pratiyāsyasi
english: "Fight, if you are a hero, O son of Rāvaṇa, O fool! Having come against the son of the Wind, you shall not return alive."

sanskrit: bāhubhyāṃ saṃprayudhyasva yadi me dvandvam āhave vegaṃ sahasva durbuddhe tatas tvaṃ rakṣasāṃ varaḥ
english: "Fight with your bare arms if you desire single combat with me in battle — bear my speed, O dim-wit! Then you would indeed be the foremost among rākṣasas."

sanskrit: hanūmantaṃ jighāṃsantaṃ samudyataśarāsanam rāvaṇātmajam ācaṣṭe lakṣmaṇāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Vibhīṣaṇa pointed out to Lakṣmaṇa the son of Rāvaṇa, intent on killing Hanumān and with his bow raised.

sanskrit: yas tu vāsavanirjetā rāvaṇasyātmasaṃbhavaḥ sa eṣa ratham āsthāya hanūmantaṃ jighāṃsati
english: "He who conquered Vāsava [Indra], the very son born of Rāvaṇa himself — that one has mounted his chariot and seeks to kill Hanumān."

sanskrit: tam apratimasaṃsthānaiḥ śaraiḥ śatruvidāraṇaiḥ jīvitāntakarair ghoraiḥ saumitre rāvaṇiṃ jahi
english: "Slay Rāvaṇi, O son of Sumitrā, with arrows of incomparable form, enemy-rending, life-ending, and dreadful."

sanskrit: ity evam uktas tu tadā mahātmā vibhīṣaṇenārivibhīṣaṇena dadarśa taṃ parvatasaṃnikāśaṃ rathasthitaṃ bhīmabalaṃ durāsadam
english: Thus spoken to then by the great-souled Vibhīṣaṇa, who is terror to foes, he beheld Rāvaṇi stationed in his chariot — that one resembling a mountain, of fearful power, hard to approach.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu saumitriṃ jātaharṣo vibhīṣaṇaḥ dhanuṣpāṇinam ādāya tvaramāṇo jagāma saḥ
english: Having thus addressed the son of Sumitrā, the joyful Vibhīṣaṇa, taking him who had his bow in hand, went in haste.

sanskrit: avidūraṃ tato gatvā praviśya ca mahad vanam darśayām āsa tat karma lakṣmaṇāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Going not far from there and entering the great forest, Vibhīṣaṇa revealed that act to Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: nīlajīmūtasaṃkāśaṃ nyagrodhaṃ bhīmadarśanam tejasvī rāvaṇabhrātā lakṣmaṇāya nyavedayat
english: The brother of Rāvaṇa, full of radiance, pointed out to Lakṣmaṇa a banyan tree resembling a dark rain-cloud, terrible to behold.

sanskrit: ihopahāraṃ bhūtānāṃ balavān rāvaṇātmajaḥ upahṛtya tataḥ paścāt saṃgrāmam abhivartate
english: "Here the mighty son of Rāvaṇa offers oblations to the spirits, and thereafter advances to battle."

sanskrit: adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati rākṣasaḥ nihanti samare śatrūn badhnāti ca śarottamaiḥ
english: "After that, the rākṣasa becomes invisible to all beings; he slays enemies in battle and binds them with excellent arrows."

sanskrit: tam apraviṣṭaṃ nyagrodhaṃ balinaṃ rāvaṇātmajam vidhvaṃsaya śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ sarathaṃ sāśvasārathim
english: "Before the mighty son of Rāvaṇa enters the banyan tree, destroy him together with his chariot, horses, and charioteer, with sharp arrows."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā mahātejāḥ saumitrir mitranandanaḥ babhūvāvasthitas tatra citraṃ visphārayan dhanuḥ
english: Saying "So be it," the great-spirited son of Sumitrā, the delight of his friends, stood there twanging his wonderful bow.

sanskrit: sa rathenāgnivarṇena balavān rāvaṇātmajaḥ indrajit kavacī khaḍgī sadhvajaḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Then the mighty son of Rāvaṇa, Indrajit, became visible there in his chariot the colour of fire, clad in armour, bearing a sword, with his banner raised.

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejāḥ paulastyam aparājitam samāhvaye tvāṃ samare samyag yuddhaṃ prayaccha me
english: The great-spirited one spoke to that undefeated descendant of Pulastya: "I challenge you in battle — give me a proper fight!"

sanskrit: evam ukto mahātejā manasvī rāvaṇātmajaḥ abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇam
english: Thus addressed, the great-spirited and noble son of Rāvaṇa spoke harsh words there, having seen Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: iha tvaṃ jātasaṃvṛddhaḥ sākṣād bhrātā pitur mama kathaṃ druhyasi putrasya pitṛvyo mama rākṣasa
english: "You were born and raised here; you are in truth the brother of my father — how can you work against your nephew's son, O rākṣasa? You are my uncle!"

sanskrit: na jñātitvaṃ na sauhārdaṃ na jātis tava durmate pramāṇaṃ na ca sodaryaṃ na dharmo dharmadūṣaṇa
english: "Kinship is no authority for you, nor friendship, nor birth, nor brotherhood, nor dharma — O defiler of dharma, O fool!"

sanskrit: śocyas tvam asi durbuddhe nindanīyaś ca sādhubhiḥ yas tvaṃ svajanam utsṛjya parabhṛtyatvam āgataḥ
english: "You are pitiable, O fool, and censured by the righteous — you who, abandoning your own kin, have come to serve others."

sanskrit: naitac chithilayā buddhyā tvaṃ vetsi mahad antaram kva ca svajanasaṃvāsaḥ kva ca nīcaparāśrayaḥ
english: "With your slack intellect you do not know the great difference — what a thing it is to dwell with one's own kin, and what a thing to take refuge with the base!"

sanskrit: guṇavān vā parajanaḥ svajano nirguṇo 'pi vā nirguṇaḥ svajanaḥ śreyān yaḥ paraḥ para eva saḥ
english: "Whether the stranger be virtuous or one's own kin be without virtue, a kinsman without virtue is still better — for a stranger is a stranger indeed."

sanskrit: niranukrośatā ceyaṃ yādṛśī te niśācara svajanena tvayā śakyaṃ paruṣaṃ rāvaṇānuja
english: "And this pitilessness of yours, O night-wanderer, O younger brother of Rāvaṇa — that you can speak harshly against your own kind!"

sanskrit: ity ukto bhrātṛputreṇa pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ ajānann iva macchīlaṃ kiṃ rākṣasa vikatthase
english: Thus addressed by his brother's son, Vibhīṣaṇa replied: "As if unknowing of my character — why do you boast, O rākṣasa?"

sanskrit: rākṣasendrasutāsādho pāruṣyaṃ tyaja gauravāt kule yady apy ahaṃ jāto rakṣasāṃ krūrakarmaṇām guṇo 'yaṃ prathamo nṝṇāṃ tan me śīlam arākṣasaṃ
english: "O son of the lord of rākṣasas, O wicked one — abandon harshness out of respect. Though I was born in a lineage of rākṣasas of cruel deeds, this is indeed the first virtue of men; and therefore my character is free of rākṣasa-nature."

sanskrit: na rame dāruṇenāhaṃ na cādharmeṇa vai rame bhrātrā viṣamaśīlena kathaṃ bhrātā nirasyate
english: "I do not delight in cruelty; I do not delight in unrighteousness. How can a brother be abandoned because of a brother's uneven conduct?"

sanskrit: parasvānāṃ ca haraṇaṃ paradārābhimarśanam suhṛdām atiśaṅkāṃ ca trayo doṣāḥ kṣayāvahāḥ
english: "The seizure of others' wealth, the violation of others' wives, and excessive suspicion of friends — these three faults bring ruin."

sanskrit: maharṣīṇāṃ vadho ghoraḥ sarvadevaiś ca vigrahaḥ abhimānaś ca kopaś ca vairitvaṃ pratikūlatā
english: "The dreadful slaughter of great seers, conflict with all the gods, arrogance, anger, making enemies, and contrariness —"

sanskrit: ete doṣā mama bhrātur jīvitaiśvaryanāśanāḥ guṇān pracchādayām āsuḥ parvatān iva toyadāḥ
english: "— these faults of my brother, which destroy life and sovereignty, have covered over his virtues as rain-clouds cover the mountains."

sanskrit: doṣair etaiḥ parityakto mayā bhrātā pitā tava neyam asti purī laṅkā na ca tvaṃ na ca te pitā
english: "Because of these faults I have abandoned the brother who is your father. This city of Laṅkā is nothing, and neither are you, nor is your father."

sanskrit: atimānī ca bālaś ca durvinītaś ca rākṣasa baddhas tvaṃ kālapāśena brūhi māṃ yad yad icchasi
english: "You are arrogant, immature, and ill-bred, O rākṣasa; you are bound by the noose of Time — say to me whatever you wish."

sanskrit: adya te vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ kim iha tvaṃ tu vakṣyasi praveṣṭuṃ na tvayā śakyo nyagrodho rākṣasādhama
english: "Today disaster has come upon you — what more will you say here? You will not be able to enter the banyan tree, O vilest of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: dharṣayitvā tu kākutsthau na śakyaṃ jīvituṃ tvayā yudhyasva naradevena lakṣmaṇena raṇe saha hatas tvaṃ devatā kāryaṃ kariṣyasi yamakṣaye
english: "Having offended the two descendants of Kakutstha, you cannot live. Fight in battle with the god among men, Lakṣmaṇa; slain, you will serve the gods' purpose in Yama's realm."

sanskrit: nidarśayasvātmabalaṃ samudyataṃ kuruṣva sarvāyudhasāyakavyayam na lakṣmaṇasyaitya hi bāṇagocaraṃ tvam adya jīvan sabalo gamiṣyasi
english: "Show your own strength, fully roused; expend all your weapons and arrows. Having come within range of Lakṣmaṇa's arrows today, you and your forces shall not go away alive."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇa vacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ vegenābhyutpapāta ha
english: Having heard Vibhīṣaṇa's words, Rāvaṇi, stupefied with fury, spoke harsh words and leaped forward with speed.

sanskrit: udyatāyudhanistriṃśo rathe tu samalaṃkṛte kālāśvayukte mahati sthitaḥ kālāntakopamaḥ
english: Standing in the great, well-adorned chariot yoked with black horses, his weapon and sword raised, he resembled Death, the Ender, in his wrath.

sanskrit: mahāpramāṇam udyamya vipulaṃ vegavad dṛḍham dhanur bhīmaṃ parāmṛśya śarāṃś cāmitranāśanān
english: Taking up his great-sized, broad, swift, strong, and dreadful bow, and grasping arrows that destroy enemies —

sanskrit: uvācainaṃ samārabdhaḥ saumitriṃ savibhīṣaṇam tāṃś ca vānaraśārdūlān paśyadhvaṃ me parākramam
english: — he, filled with fury, addressed the son of Sumitrā along with Vibhīṣaṇa and those tiger-like monkeys: "Witness my prowess!"

sanskrit: adya matkārmukotsṛṣṭaṃ śaravarṣaṃ durāsadam muktaṃ varṣam ivākāśe vārayiṣyatha saṃyuge
english: "Today in battle will you ward off the shower of arrows loosed from my bow — hard to face, like rain released into the sky?"

sanskrit: adya vo māmakā bāṇā mahākārmukaniḥsṛtāḥ vidhamiṣyanti gātrāṇi tūlarāśim ivānalaḥ
english: "Today my arrows, issuing from my great bow, will scatter your limbs as fire does a heap of cotton."

sanskrit: tīkṣṇasāyakanirbhinnāñ śūlaśaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ adya vo gamayiṣyāmi sarvān eva yamakṣayam
english: "Pierced by sharp arrows, by tridents, śaktis, ṛṣṭis, and tomaras, I will today send you all to Yama's abode."

sanskrit: kṣipataḥ śaravarṣāṇi kṣiprahastasya me yudhi jīmūtasyeva nadataḥ kaḥ sthāsyati mamāgrataḥ
english: "Who will stand before me in battle as I rain down showers of arrows with my swift hand, roaring like a rain-cloud?"

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rākṣasendrasya garjitaṃ lakṣmaṇas tadā abhītavadanaḥ kruddho rāvaṇiṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing that roar of the lord of rākṣasas, Lakṣmaṇa then with fearless face, filled with anger, spoke these words to Rāvaṇi.

sanskrit: uktaś ca durgamaḥ pāraḥ kāryāṇāṃ rākṣasa tvayā kāryāṇāṃ karmaṇā pāraṃ yo gacchati sa buddhimān
english: "You have spoken of the far shore of deeds as hard to reach, O rākṣasa; but he is the wise one who reaches the far shore of deeds by action itself."

sanskrit: sa tvam arthasya hīnārtho duravāpasya kena cit vaco vyāhṛtya jānīṣe kṛtārtho 'smīti durmate
english: "You, who fall short of the goal, having spoken words about a purpose hard for anyone to attain, consider yourself accomplished — O fool!"

sanskrit: antardhānagatenājau yas tvayācaritas tadā taskarācarito mārgo naiṣa vīraniṣevitaḥ
english: "The way you practised in battle back then — going invisible — that is the path followed by thieves; it is not the path heroes follow."

sanskrit: yathā bāṇapathaṃ prāpya sthito 'haṃ tava rākṣasa darśayasvādya tat tejo vācā tvaṃ kiṃ vikatthase
english: "Even as I stand here within range of your arrows, O rākṣasa — reveal that power today. Why do you boast only with words?"

sanskrit: evam ukto dhanur bhīmaṃ parāmṛśya mahābalaḥ sasarje niśitān bāṇān indrajit samijiṃjaya
english: Thus addressed, the mighty Indrajit, grasping his dreadful bow, released sharp arrows, victorious in battle.

sanskrit: te nisṛṣṭā mahāvegāḥ śarāḥ sarpaviṣopamāḥ saṃprāpya lakṣmaṇaṃ petuḥ śvasanta iva pannagāḥ
english: Those arrows, released with great speed, equal to serpent-venom, reached Lakṣmaṇa and fell upon him as if hissing like snakes.

sanskrit: śarair atimahāvegair vegavān rāvaṇātmajaḥ saumitrim indrajid yuddhe vivyādha śubhalakṣaṇam
english: The swift son of Rāvaṇa, Indrajit, pierced in battle with arrows of very great speed the auspiciously-marked son of Sumitrā.

sanskrit: sa śarair atividdhāṅgo rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ śuśubhe lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmān vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: His limbs deeply pierced by arrows and drenched in blood, the glorious Lakṣmaṇa shone like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: indrajit tv ātmanaḥ karma prasamīkṣyādhigamya ca vinadya sumahānādam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Indrajit, observing his own feat and exulting in it, let out a very great roar and spoke these words.

sanskrit: patriṇaḥ śitadhārās te śarā matkārmukacyutāḥ ādāsyante 'dya saumitre jīvitaṃ jīvitāntagāḥ
english: "These feathered, keen-edged arrows released from my bow, life-ending, will take your life today, O son of Sumitrā!"

sanskrit: adya gomāyusaṃghāś ca śyenasaṃghāś ca lakṣmaṇa gṛdhrāś ca nipatantu tvāṃ gatāsuṃ nihataṃ mayā
english: "Today let the packs of jackals, the flocks of hawks, and the vultures descend upon you, O Lakṣmaṇa — lifeless, slain by me!"

sanskrit: kṣatrabandhuḥ sadānāryo rāmaḥ paramadurmatiḥ bhaktaṃ bhrātaram adyaiva tvāṃ drakṣyati mayā hatam
english: "Rāma, ever noble, a mere kshatriya-aspirant, of utterly confused mind, will today see you his devoted brother — slain by me!"

sanskrit: viśastakavacaṃ bhūmau vyapaviddhaśarāsanam hṛtottamāṅgaṃ saumitre tvām adya nihataṃ mayā
english: "Your armour shattered, your bow cast aside on the ground, your head severed, O son of Sumitrā — today I shall slay you!"

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ paruṣaṃ rāvaṇātmajam hetumadvākyam atyarthaṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ pratyuvāca ha
english: As the son of Rāvaṇa spoke thus, furious and harsh, Lakṣmaṇa replied to him with words exceedingly reasoned.

sanskrit: akṛtvā katthase karma kimartham iha rākṣasa kuru tat karma yenāhaṃ śraddadhyāṃ tava katthanam
english: "Without accomplishing the deed, why do you boast here, O rākṣasa? Do that deed by which I would believe your boasting."

sanskrit: anuktvā paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ kiṃ cid apy anavakṣipan avikatthan vadhiṣyāmi tvāṃ paśya puruṣādana
english: "Without speaking a single harsh word, without belittling you, without boasting, I will slay you — watch, O devourer of men!"

sanskrit: ity uktvā pañcanārācān ākarṇāpūritāñ śarān nicakhāna mahāvegāṃl lakṣmaṇo rākṣasorasi
english: Having spoken thus, Lakṣmaṇa drove five iron-tipped arrows, drawn to his ear and of great velocity, deep into the rākṣasa's chest.

sanskrit: sa śarair āhatas tena saroṣo rāvaṇātmajaḥ suprayuktais tribhir bāṇaiḥ prativivyādha lakṣmaṇam
english: Struck by those arrows, the son of Rāvaṇa, filled with rage, pierced Lakṣmaṇa in return with three well-aimed arrows.

sanskrit: sa babhūva mahābhīmo nararākṣasasiṃhayoḥ vimardas tumulo yuddhe parasparavadhaiṣiṇoḥ
english: There arose a most dreadful and tumultuous combat in battle between those two lions — the man and the rākṣasa — each seeking to slay the other.

sanskrit: ubhau hi balasaṃpannāv ubhau vikramaśālinau ubhāv api suvikrāntau sarvaśastrāstrakovidau
english: Both were possessed of great strength, both were endowed with valour, both were supremely courageous, and both were skilled in all weapons and missiles.

sanskrit: ubhau paramadurjeyāv atulyabalatejasau yuyudhāte mahāvīrau grahāv iva nabho gatau
english: Both supremely hard to conquer, both of incomparable strength and splendour, those two great heroes fought like two planets colliding in the sky.

sanskrit: balavṛtrāv iva hi tau yudhi vai duṣpradharṣaṇau yuyudhāte mahātmānau tadā kesariṇāv iva
english: Like Bala and Vṛtra, those two great-souled ones, truly invincible in battle, fought like two lions.

sanskrit: bahūn avasṛjantau hi mārgaṇaughān avasthitau nararākṣasasiṃhau tau prahṛṣṭāv abhyayudhyatām
english: Releasing many torrents of arrows as they stood firm, those two lions — the man and the rākṣasa — fought with great exhilaration.

sanskrit: susaṃprahṛṣṭau nararākṣasottamau jayaiṣiṇau mārgaṇacāpadhāriṇau parasparaṃ tau pravavarṣatur bhṛśaṃ śaraughavarṣeṇa balāhakāv iva
english: Greatly exhilarated, those two foremost beings — man and rākṣasa — each seeking victory, bearing arrows and bows, rained heavily upon each other with floods of arrows, like two rain-clouds.
